title: Putin signs treaties annexing four occupied Ukrainian regions
body:
On Friday, 30 September 2022, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed treaties at the Kremlin in Moscow formally annexing four Ukrainian regions that Russian troops occupy: Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk and Luhansk. The Russian-installed and separatist leaders of the regions, Vladimir Saldo, Yevgeny Balitsky, Denis Pushilin and Leonid Pasechnik, took part in the ceremony.

Putin described the annexation as irreversible and said the people of these regions were becoming citizens of Russia forever, defying efforts by Kyiv, backed by the United States and its allies, to retake the territory. The treaties followed votes held from 23 to 27 September that Ukraine and Western governments rejected. They were then to go to Russia's Constitutional Court, the State Duma and the Federal Council.

The ceremony was held in the Kremlin's St George's Hall. In his speech Putin urged Kyiv to negotiate while warning that Russia would defend the regions it now declared to be its own. Ukraine, the United States, the European Union and other Western governments said they would not recognise the annexations, which they described as violations of international law. The four oblasts were only partly under Russian control at the time of the signing, and Ukrainian forces continued operations in several of them in the following days, including at Lyman in Donetsk Oblast, which Russian troops left on 1 October 2022.
